songInfo.title: The Boys Are Back in Town
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

scalesUsed.notes: Ab - Bb - C - Db - Eb - F - G
scalesUsed.application: Drives the joyous, uplifting main riff and the iconic twin-guitar harmonized lines (played as A major shapes on downtuned guitars)
Provides the melodic skeleton for Scott Gorham and Brian Robertson's singing lead fills

scalesUsed.notes: F - G - Ab - Bb - C - Db - Eb
scalesUsed.application: Relative minor scale that adds soulful bluesy melancholy to the verse and bridge turnarounds

keyAndScale.keySignature: Four flats (Bb, Eb, Ab, Db) (concert Ab major; written as A major with three sharps in half-step down tuning)

mainProgression.description: A swinging, soulful classic rock anthem. Phil Lynott's swaggering bass groove anchors the classic Mixolydian I - bVII - IV - I progression, over which Gorham and Robertson weave harmonized third and sixth counterpoints.

sectionProgressions.description: Twin Les Paul guitars playing diatonic thirds in perfect lockstep, punctuated by swinging syncopated snare cracks
Bouncy, soulful progression driven by syncopated palm muting and rhythmic chord comping
'The boys are back in town! The boys are back in town!' - triumphant unmuted power chords ringing with anthemic energy
Soulful minor-key interlude setting up Lynott's storytelling verses and soaring lead guitar fills

harmonicFunction: Ab (I) - Warm, triumphant tonic chord establishing the joyful camaraderie and Irish soul
Gb (bVII) - Subtonic Mixolydian chord injecting classic rock grit and forward momentum
Db (IV) - Subdominant chord providing uplifting major resolution in the chorus climb
Eb (V) - Dominant chord delivering harmonic tension pulling back to the tonic Ab
Cm (iii) - Mediant chord providing sweet, melancholic inner-voice motion in the verse

techniques.name: Twin-Guitar Diatonic Third Harmonization
techniques.description: Scott Gorham and Brian Robertson's signature dual-lead interplay, playing diatonic thirds with identical pick attack, matching vibrato width, and synchronized position slides

notes: Upper guitar plays the primary melody while the second guitar harmonizes a diatonic third below
Both players must align their pick attacks down to the exact millisecond
Apply wide, singing finger vibrato from the wrist simultaneously
Dampen strings cleanly at phrase conclusions so note cutoffs match in flawless unison
sequence: Lead guitar picks fret 9 on G string while harmony guitar picks fret 7 on D string (concert Ab)
Both slide two frets higher into diatonic third harmony
Execute syncopated descending triplets across strings 2 and 3
Resolve together onto the root-third dyad
tips: When learning alone, record one harmony line on a looper pedal or DAW, then practice locking the second voice over top
Tune carefully to half-step down: looser strings mean bends require less pressure but intonation must be monitored
Use Les Paul bridge humbuckers through cranked Marshall amps for rich, singing overtone sustain

techniques.name: Syncopated R&B Rock Chugging
techniques.description: Bouncy, syncopated rhythm comping combining light palm muting on the lower registers with snappy upstroke chord stabs that lock in the swinging pocket behind Phil Lynott's bass

notes: Rest the heel of your pick hand lightly on the bridge for percussive string control
Emphasize the swing feel on eighth notes: long-short-long-short rhythmic subdivision
Accentuate the offbeat upstrokes on beats 2-and and 4-and
Release fret-hand pressure immediately to achieve crisp staccato chord duration
sequence: Chug muted root on low strings
Snap the upper triad on the upbeat with a crisp upstroke
Slide fret-hand shape two frets down for the bVII chord change
Lock into the 120 BPM swinging groove
tips: Think like a rhythm-and-blues rhythm guitarist: keep your pick hand bouncing in continuous motion
Roll guitar volume back slightly to 7 to clean up chord separation in the verses
Listen to Phil Lynott's bassline: the guitar should sit right in the pocket on top of the bass groove

sections.name: Intro Signature Twin-Lead Fanfare
sections.description: One of classic rock's most joyous and recognizable guitar hooks: dual Gibson Les Pauls harmonize in sweet diatonic thirds over Brian Downey's swinging drum groove at 120 BPM.
notes: Flawless unison pick attack between lead and harmony guitars
Slide into the opening major 3rd interval with confidence
Match note cutoffs and vibrato rate identically
Let the swing feel bounce naturally without rushing

sections.name: Verse 1 Soulful Staccato Groove
sections.description: 'Guess who just got back today? Them wild-eyed boys that had been away...' - relaxed, swinging rhythm guitar comping behind Phil Lynott's charismatic vocal.
notes: Light palm muting on the downbeats
Snap upstrokes on the syncopated offbeats
Smooth transitions between Ab and the soulful Cm chord
Keep fret-hand pressure relaxed to maintain groove stamina

sections.name: Chorus Stadium Anthem
sections.description: 'The boys are back in town! The boys are back in town!' - full unmuted power chords and roaring dual guitars deliver the immortal stadium chorus.
notes: Open up the pick hand for big, ringing chords
Accentuate beats 2 and 4 with heavy downstrokes
Lead guitar doubles vocal melodies with short pentatonic fills
Dynamic crescendo leading into the second verse

sections.name: Bridge Storytelling Breakdown
sections.description: 'That chick that's down on Dino's Bar & Grill...' - atmospheric minor breakdown providing dramatic emotional contrast before the twin-guitar solo.
notes: Delicate chord strums allowing Lynott's storytelling vocal to shine
Subtle electric guitar volume swells and arpeggios
Ascending chromatic bassline building tension
Explosive drum fill into the twin guitar solo

sections.name: Twin Guitar Harmonized Solo
sections.description: Gorham and Robertson take center stage: an electrifying harmonized dual guitar solo featuring descending runs, syncopated triplets, and singing vibrato in glorious thirds.
notes: Twin lines trace descending diatonic thirds across frets 9, 11, and 13
Execute unison whole-step bends on fret 11 of the G string and fret 13 of the B string
Maintain absolute synchronization of pick attack and vibrato
End with climbing major pentatonic fanfare into the chorus

sections.name: Outro Jam & Twin Lead Extravaganza
sections.description: Continuous, joyous twin-lead guitar celebration repeating the main harmonized fanfare while Gorham and Robertson trade melodic flourishes to a fading studio resolve.
notes: Both guitars interlock in non-stop harmonized counterpoint
High-energy drum fills support the driving 120 BPM tempo
Playful blues bends and slide flourishes on the fading vamp
Smooth, singing studio fadeout

guitar.recommended: Gibson Les Paul Deluxe with mini-humbuckers or Les Paul Standard
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for cutting, articulate midrange crunch

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP 50W or 100W Super Lead pushed into vintage tube saturation

effects.distortion: Colorsound overdriver or natural Marshall power tube saturation
effects.other: MXR Phase 90 on subtle passages and light analog tape delay (150ms slapback)

beginner.title: Chords & Swing Rhythm
steps: Tune your guitar half-step down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)
Learn open and barre chord shapes for Ab, Gb, and Db
Practice counting the 120 BPM swinging 4/4 shuffle rhythm

intermediate.title: Main Harmonized Theme & Comping
steps: Learn the upper voice of the signature intro theme
Practice syncopated verse comping with clean offbeat upstrokes
Master the transition from verse palm muting to chorus strumming

advanced.title: Full Twin Harmonization & Complete Solo
steps: Learn both upper and lower voices of the harmonized solo and outro
Coordinate identical vibrato speed, depth, and pick attack with a partner or looper
Perform the entire track maintaining flawless swing timing and tone

commonMistakes: Playing in standard tuning instead of half-step down, resulting in clashing key pitch
Rushing the swing feel and turning the soulful shuffle into a stiff, straight eighth-note march
Mismatched vibrato and bends during the twin-lead harmony passages
Using too much distortion, muddying the clean diatonic third separation
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Half-step down tuning check and gentle finger warm-up
10 mins: Slow metronome repetition of the twin-lead intro theme at 85, 105, and 120 BPM
10 mins: Syncopated verse comping and offbeat upstroke drills
10 mins: Twin-lead solo transcription practice over a looper pedal or backing track
focusAreas: Twin-guitar unison synchronization and vibrato alignment
Swinging shuffle rhythm and syncopated upbeat accents
Tone balance and dynamic separation between dual guitars
metronomeWork: Set your metronome to 120 BPM with a triplet swing click to feel the authentic shuffle pocket
Practice the intro twin lead at 85 BPM until every slide and cutoff is second nature
Isolate the bridge-to-solo transition to ensure the tempo never rushes on the entrance
